summary: Three-phase plan to add check_deployed_rule_drift() to check-extension-docs.sh as a near-verbatim mirror of check_deployed_script_drift(), wired into the per-extension dispatch block next to check_undeclared_rules. Phase 1 captures a pre-change baseline (measured at plan time: exit 0, 'PASS: all extensions OK', two script copies byte-identical). Phase 2 adds and wires the function with a mandatory dual write to both .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh and .claude/extensions/core/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh. Phase 3 runs the script and asserts exit-code parity with the baseline, expected per-extension pass/skip behavior of the new check, and absence of self-drift, plus a revertible negative-path check proving the new check actually detects drift. The plan records the decision NOT to parameterize a cross-category helper for provides.agents/commands/context, with justification (agents needs an agents_subdir parameter; context needs recursive directory comparison; no second caller exists yet) and an explicit revisit trigger.

artifacts.summary: Three-phase implementation plan (baseline capture -> dual-write implementation -> baseline-compared verification) for the extension rule drift check, with the no-parameterization decision recorded durably and the self-referential dual-write hazard called out in every editing phase.

next_action_hint: Run /implement 861 to execute the plan. Implementation must dual-write every script edit to both .claude/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh and .claude/extensions/core/scripts/check-extension-docs.sh, or the script's own drift check will flag the change itself.
